# RADS - CBA Settings

<!-- generated by tools/gen_settings.py -->

All settings live under **Addon Options > RADS - Adaptive Detection**. Every value is read live, so a change made mid-mission applies at the next evaluation. All settings are server settings: only the server (or a logged-in admin) can change them and clients cannot override them. The only exception is the debug options marked *per player*, and players can only use those when the server's 'Who may use debug' allows it. Hover a setting in game for the same explanation; the reset button shows its default.

Runtime overrides from the Zeus/3DEN **Detection Settings** modules or `root_ads_fnc_setOverride` take precedence over these values until cleared. Variable names are `root_ads_main_<name>`.

Multipliers: 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = suspicion builds twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.

## Basics

| Setting | Name | Default | Range / options | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enable RADS | `enabled` | on |  | Master switch for the whole undercover system. Off = every player is back to normal Arma detection right away (AI shoot on sight). |
| BLUFOR can go undercover | `coverWest` | on |  | BLUFOR players (and their AI passengers) can hide their identity inside vehicles. Off = BLUFOR is always detected normally. |
| OPFOR can go undercover | `coverEast` | on |  | OPFOR players can hide their identity inside vehicles. Turn on when OPFOR is the player side. |
| INDFOR can go undercover | `coverGuer` | on |  | Independent players can hide their identity inside vehicles. Turn on when INDFOR is the player side. |
| Cover AI passengers | `coverAIPassengers` | on |  | AI soldiers of a covered side riding with an undercover player are undercover too. Off = enemy AI shoot at the vehicle because of the AI passenger. |
| Check every (s) | `tickInterval` | 1 | 0.25 - 5 | How often each enemy group re-checks every undercover player. Lower = reacts faster but costs more CPU. Higher = cheaper but jumpier. Example: 1 = once per second (recommended). |
| Groups checked per frame | `groupsPerFrame` | 6 | 1 - 50 | Performance budget: how many enemy groups are checked in a single frame. Lower = smoother frame rate with many AI. Higher = every group is updated sooner. Leave at 6 unless you have hundreds of AI groups. |
| Maximum spotting range (m) | `maxRange` | 800 | 50 - 3000 | Enemy AI farther away than this can never become suspicious of a vehicle. Lower = drive past distant positions freely. Higher = long-range observers matter. Example: 800 = a sniper team 1 km away ignores you. |
| Observers checked per group | `maxObservers` | 4 | 1 - 12 | How many soldiers of each group (closest to the vehicle first) get a line-of-sight check. Higher = more accurate in big groups, costs more CPU. |

## Who and What Gets Cover

| Setting | Name | Default | Range / options | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Civilian vehicles give cover | `allowCivVeh` | on |  | Civilian cars, trucks, boats and aircraft disguise the people inside. Off = civilian vehicles do not hide anyone. |
| Enemy-owned vehicles give cover | `allowFriendlyVeh` | on |  | Vehicles of the watching AI's own or allied side disguise the people inside. Example: BLUFOR players in a captured OPFOR truck fool OPFOR. |
| Own-side vehicles give cover | `allowHostileVeh` | All vehicles | Never / Unarmed vehicles only / All vehicles | Vehicles of a side the watching AI is at war with can still disguise the people inside, but suspicion builds much faster (see 'Vehicle Faction'). Example: BLUFOR players in an unarmed BLUFOR Hunter at an OPFOR checkpoint. |
| Aircraft give cover | `allowAir` | on |  | Helicopters and planes can disguise the people inside. Off = aircraft never give cover. |
| Boats give cover | `allowBoats` | on |  | Boats can disguise the people inside. Off = boats never give cover. |
| Open vehicles (quads, bikes...) | `openVehicleMode` | No cover | Cover, but easy to spot / No cover | What happens in vehicles where everyone can see you (quad bikes, motorbikes, open boats). |
| Open vehicle classes | `openVehicleClasses` | `Quadbike_01_base_F,Kart_01_Base_F,Motorcycle,Bicycle,Rubber_duck_base_F,LSV_01_light_base_F,LSV_02_unarmed_base_F` |  | Comma-separated vehicle classes treated as open vehicles. Child classes are included. Example: Quadbike_01_base_F,Motorcycle |
| Always-disguise vehicles | `vehWhitelist` | (empty) |  | Comma-separated vehicle classes that always disguise, whatever their side. Example: C_Van_01_transport_F |
| Never-disguise vehicles | `vehBlacklist` | (empty) |  | Comma-separated vehicle classes that never disguise anyone. Example: B_MRAP_01_F (the Hunter is too obviously NATO). |
| Uncovered people in the vehicle | `mixedCrewMode` | Faster suspicion | Ignore / Faster suspicion / Nobody has cover | What happens when someone in the vehicle has no cover (an exempt player, AI of another side). |
| Leave captive units alone | `captiveStandDown` | on |  | If a mission or another undercover script makes a unit captive, RADS ignores it. Keep on when combining RADS with other undercover scripts. |

## Getting Into a Vehicle

| Setting | Name | Default | Range / options | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Witness knowledge | `witnessKA` | 1.5 | 0 - 4 | A group that knows you this well (0-4, the engine's knowsAbout) and saw you just before you got in keeps full knowledge: getting into a car in front of them does not fool them. |
| Witness window (s) | `witnessWindow` | 6 | 0 - 60 | A group that saw you within this many seconds before you got in counts as a witness. |
| Combat window (s) | `combatWindow` | 20 | 0 - 180 | A group you fought within this many seconds keeps fighting you after you get in. |
| Earlier knowledge becomes suspicion | `seedFactor` | 50% | 0-100% | Share of a group's earlier (non-witness) knowledge of you that turns into starting suspicion when you get in. 0 = a clean slate every time. 1 = what they knew carries over fully. |
| Searching groups build faster | `searchingBuildMult` | 1.5 | 1 - 5 | Suspicion speed for groups that are already SEARCHING for you. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast. |
| Entry sync delay (s) | `coverGraceTime` | 2 | 0 - 5 | Technical: other machines wait this long after you get in before judging you, so the entry snapshot is used. Leave at 2 unless told otherwise. |

## How Fast Suspicion Builds

| Setting | Name | Default | Range / options | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Base build speed (%/s) | `buildRate` | 12 | 1 - 100 | Suspicion gained per second when an alert soldier gets a clear look at you up close. Higher = identified faster. Lower = more time to pass through. Example: 12 = about 8 s of a clear close look from 0 to 100%. |
| Calm-down speed (%/s) | `decayRate` | 1.5 | 0 - 50 | Suspicion lost per second while nobody in the group can see you. Higher = they forget you fast. Lower = they stay wary longer. Example: 1.5 = from 60% back to 0% in 40 s out of sight. |
| Suspicious at (%) | `suspiciousThreshold` | 35 | 1 - 99 | At this suspicion the group becomes SUSPICIOUS: it may go alert, watch you, and you get a warning hint. Lower = they react to you earlier. |
| Identified at (%) | `identifyThreshold` | 100 | 10 - 100 | At this suspicion the group sees through your disguise and attacks. Lower = cover breaks sooner. 100 = only at full suspicion. |
| Close look range (m) | `identifyRange` | 40 | 5 - 500 | Within this distance the AI sees you just as well as up close. Farther away it gets harder fast. Higher = suspicion builds from farther away. Example: 40 = full effect inside 40 m. |
| Distance falloff | `distanceCurve` | 1.5 | 0.25 - 4 | How quickly seeing you gets harder beyond the close look range: (close range / distance) ^ this. Higher = distance protects you more. Example: 1.5 with 40 m: 35% as effective at 80 m, 9% at 200 m, 3% at 400 m. |
| Face-to-face range (m) | `instantRange` | 6 | 0 - 100 | Within this distance a soldier is looking straight into the vehicle (checkpoint, walking past). Higher = the face-to-face bonus starts farther away. |
| Face-to-face multiplier | `instantMult` | 2 | 1 - 10 | How much faster suspicion builds inside face-to-face range. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast. Example: 4 = a guard at your window is four times as effective. |
| Face-to-face minimum visibility | `minCloseExposure` | 25% | 0-100% | How well a guard at face-to-face range sees you even through a closed body (they can lean in). 0 = a closed hull fully protects. 1 = always seen perfectly up close. |
| Vehicle body blocks sight | `hullBlocks` | on |  | Line of sight respects the vehicle itself: glass lets some sight through, doors and roof block it. Off = only terrain and buildings block sight, the vehicle is see-through. |
| Loitering ramp time (s) | `stationaryTime` | 30 | 5 - 300 | How long you must stay parked near a group before the loitering penalty is at its maximum. Lower = parking near the enemy becomes suspicious sooner. |
| Loitering maximum multiplier | `stationaryMult` | 2.5 | 1 - 5 | How much faster suspicion builds when parked near a group for the full ramp time. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast. |
| Repeated pass bonus | `passBonus` | 0.25 | 0 - 2 | Extra suspicion speed for each separate time you drive past the same group (circling, drive-bys). Example: 0.25 = second pass x1.25, third x1.5 ... |
| Repeated pass cap | `passMax` | 2.5 | 1 - 5 | The repeated pass bonus never goes above this multiplier. |
| Time between passes (s) | `passGap` | 10 | 2 - 120 | You must be out of sight this long before the next sighting counts as a new pass. |
| Enemy riding with you = identified | `sameVehicleInstant` | on |  | An enemy AI sitting in the same vehicle identifies everyone in it at once. Off = they build suspicion like everyone else. |

## What the AI Can See

| Setting | Name | Default | Range / options | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Field of view (deg) | `fovAngle` | 140 | 30 - 360 | Width of the cone a soldier is really looking at. Outside it only peripheral vision applies. Example: 140 = roughly what a person takes in without turning their head. |
| Peripheral vision | `peripheralMult` | 10% | 0-100% | How well a soldier notices you outside their field of view. 0 = not at all. 1 = as well as looking straight at you. |
| Relaxed AI (SAFE / CARELESS) | `behSafe` | 0.7 | 0 - 3 | Suspicion speed for relaxed soldiers. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast. Example: 0.7 = bored sentries are slower to notice. |
| Alert AI (AWARE) | `behAware` | 1 | 0 - 3 | Suspicion speed for alert soldiers. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast. |
| Fighting AI (COMBAT) | `behCombat` | 1.125 | 0 - 3 | Suspicion speed for soldiers in combat. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast. Lower = they are busy with the fight and pay less attention to traffic. |
| Sneaking AI (STEALTH) | `behStealth` | 1.25 | 0 - 3 | Suspicion speed for soldiers in stealth mode. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast. Higher = they are watching carefully. |
| AI skill influence | `skillInfluence` | 50% | 0-100% | How much the AI's spotting skills change suspicion speed. 0 = skill does not matter. 1 = a skilled spotter is up to twice as fast, a poor one much slower. |
| Busy fighting someone else | `engagedElsewhereMult` | 0.6 | 0 - 2 | Suspicion speed while the group is fighting another enemy. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast. |
| Vehicle optics see farther | `vehOpticsEnabled` | on |  | AI in a vehicle's gunner or commander seat (hatch closed) look through sights: they judge you from farther away. Only the range changes, not how wide they look. Turned out or firing-from-vehicle seats use their own eyes and weapons. |
| Gunner / commander optics range | `vehOpticsMult` | 1.5 | 0.25 - 5 | Range multiplier for AI behind vehicle optics. 1 = like the naked eye. Higher = they read you from farther (and suspicion builds faster at a distance). Lower = worse than the naked eye. Example: 1.5 = a BMP gunner 300 m away judges you as if you were 200 m away. Each vehicle can set its own value (Vehicle Disguise module / setVehicleMode). |
| Driver's view range | `vehDriverOpticsMult` | 0.580277 | 0.25 - 5 | Range multiplier for AI driving a vehicle (hatch closed). 1 = like the naked eye. Lower = a driver behind a vision block sees less. |

## Light and Weather

| Setting | Name | Default | Range / options | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Darkness | `nightMult` | 35% | 0-100% | How well the AI sees into vehicles in full darkness (scaled smoothly by sun and moon light). 0 = blind at night. 1 = night makes no difference. |
| Darkness with night vision | `nvgNightMult` | 85% | 0-100% | Same as Darkness, for AI wearing night vision goggles. |
| Fog | `fogInfluence` | 60% | 0-100% | How much fog hides you. 0 = fog does nothing. 1 = thick fog hides you completely. |
| Rain | `rainInfluence` | 45% | 0-100% | How much rain hides you. 0 = rain does nothing. 1 = heavy rain hides you completely. |

## Seats and Vehicle Type

| Setting | Name | Default | Range / options | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Driver seat | `seatDriver` | 1 | 0 - 3 | Suspicion speed for the driver. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast. |
| Passenger seat | `seatCargo` | 0.7 | 0 - 3 | Suspicion speed for passengers. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast. Lower = passengers in the back are harder to make out. |
| Gunner / commander seat | `seatTurret` | 1.1 | 0 - 3 | Suspicion speed for gunners and commanders inside. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast. |
| Turned out (head out of the hatch) | `seatTurnedOut` | 2.5 | 0 - 5 | Suspicion speed when turned out. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast. Higher = sticking your head out is a giveaway. |
| Firing from vehicle seat | `seatFFV` | 2.5 | 0 - 5 | Suspicion speed in seats where you hold your weapon out of the window. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast. |
| Open vehicle multiplier | `openVehicleMult` | 2.99684 | 1 - 10 | Suspicion speed on quads, bikes and other open vehicles (when they give cover). 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast. |
| Fast drive-by speed (km/h) | `fastSpeed` | 70.1479 | 10 - 200 | Above this speed the AI only get a short glimpse of you. Example: 50 = passing at 60 km/h is much safer than crawling past. |
| Fast drive-by multiplier | `fastMult` | 10% | 0-100% | Suspicion speed above the fast drive-by speed. 1 = no protection. 0.4 = 40% speed. |
| Aircraft altitude falloff (m) | `altitudeFalloff` | 200 | 10 - 1000 | Aircraft above this height get proportionally less attention. Example: 60 = at 120 m suspicion builds half as fast. |
| Damaged vehicle influence | `damageInfluence` | 2 | 0 - 5 | Visibly damaged vehicles (broken glass, bullet holes, burning) build suspicion faster: multiplier = 1 + visible damage x this. 0 = damage does not matter. |
| Suspicious on sight from damage | `damageVisibleAt` | 25% | 0-100% | A vehicle with at least this much visible damage makes the group SUSPICIOUS the moment they see it. 100% = off. |
| Damage suspicion floor | `damageFloorScale` | 60% | 0-100% | How far above 'Suspicious at' heavy damage pushes suspicion straight away. 0 = only to the suspicious level. 100% = up to just below identification for a wreck. |
| Mixed crew multiplier | `mixedCrewMult` | 1.5 | 1 - 5 | Suspicion speed for each uncovered person in the vehicle (when 'Uncovered people' = Faster suspicion). 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast. |

## Vehicle Faction

| Setting | Name | Default | Range / options | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Their own faction's vehicle | `sameFactionVehMult` | 0.5 | 0 - 3 | Suspicion speed in a vehicle of the exact faction watching you (CSAT truck at a CSAT checkpoint). 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast. Lower = they expect their own vehicles and barely look twice. |
| Their side, other faction | `friendlyVehMult` | 0.8 | 0 - 3 | Suspicion speed in a vehicle of the same side but another faction. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast. |
| Civilian vehicle | `civVehMult` | 1 | 0 - 3 | Suspicion speed in a civilian vehicle. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast. |
| Allied side's vehicle | `alliedVehMult` | 1.2 | 0 - 5 | Suspicion speed in a vehicle of a side allied to the watching AI. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast. |
| Enemy side's vehicle | `hostileVehMult` | 3 | 0 - 10 | Suspicion speed in a vehicle of a side they are at war with (only when 'Own-side vehicles give cover'). 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast. Example: 3 = a BLUFOR Hunter at an OPFOR checkpoint is identified three times as fast. |
| Per-class multipliers | `vehClassMults` | (empty) |  | Comma-separated class:multiplier pairs that replace the faction multipliers. First match wins, child classes included. Example: O_MRAP_02_F:0.4,B_MRAP_01_F:5 |

## Armored Vehicles

| Setting | Name | Default | Range / options | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Armored hulls hide the crew | `armoredDetect` | on |  | In tanks, APCs and IFVs with closed hatches the AI cannot see who is inside. They can only judge the vehicle, so suspicion builds much slower. Turned out or firing from a port = normal rules. |
| Armored vehicle classes | `armoredClasses` | `Tank,Wheeled_APC_F` |  | Comma-separated vehicle classes treated as armored (child classes included). Example: Tank,Wheeled_APC_F |
| Detect armored seats automatically | `armoredAutoDetect` | on |  | Seats that only see out through optics or periscopes (e.g. a BTR driver) count as armored even when the vehicle is not in the class list. |
| Armored hull visibility | `armoredHullMult` | 5% | 0-100% | How much of the vehicle's visibility counts while the crew sits behind armor. Lower = armored vehicles are harder to see through. 1 = no protection. Example: 0.25 = a BMP that gives itself away builds suspicion about a quarter as fast as a car. |
| Armored face-to-face | `armoredCloseMult` | 15% | 0-100% | Scales 'Face-to-face minimum visibility' for armored seats (a guard at the hull still cannot see in well). |
| Armored: only behaviour gives it away | `armoredDrivingOnly` | on |  | On = a closed armored vehicle driven calmly builds no suspicion at all (nobody can see in) and old suspicion fades. It only builds while it gives itself away: speeding or off-road near them, lights off at night, honking, pointing a gun at them, visible damage or parking next to them for long. Ramming always identifies. Off = it builds slowly from the vehicle alone (Armored hull visibility). |

Matching = item by item against what the watching side itself wears (see 'Gear Reference'). |

| Ballistic helmet | `helmetMult` | 0.99911 | 0 - 3 | Suspicion speed wearing an armored helmet. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast. |

| Same item, other camo | `gearSimilarMult` | 0.75 | 0.1 - 3 | Suspicion speed for each item of the same model but another variant (other camo). 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast. |
| Item they never wear | `gearMismatchMult` | 1.15 | 0.5 - 5 | Suspicion speed for each visible item that none of them wears. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast. Example: 1.15 with three wrong items = about 1.5x. |
| Missing item they all wear | `gearMissingMult` | 1.05 | 0.5 - 5 | Suspicion speed for each empty slot they always fill (no helmet when every guard wears one). 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast. |
| Slot weights | `gearSlotWeights` | `uniform:1.5,vest:1,headgear:1,primary:1.2,launcher:1,backpack:0.5,facewear:0.5` |  | How much each slot counts (slot:weight, comma-separated). 2 = counts double, 0 = ignored. Slots: uniform, vest, headgear, primary, launcher, backpack, facewear. |

## Driving Behaviour

## Hostile Acts

| Setting | Name | Default | Range / options | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shooting blows cover | `firedBlows` | on |  | Firing a weapon from cover gets you identified by nearby groups and by groups that see you. |
| Shot heard within (m) | `firedRadius` | 300 | 0 - 2000 | Groups within this distance of an unsuppressed shot identify the shooter. |
| Suppressed shot heard within (m) | `firedRadiusSuppressed` | 40 | 0 - 500 | Same, for suppressed weapons. |
| Seen shooting = identified | `firedLOS` | on |  | Any group with line of sight to the shooter (within spotting range) identifies them. |
| Heat after shooting (s) | `heatDuration` | 30 | 0 - 1800 | After firing you cannot regain cover for this long. 0 = off. Example: 120 = jumping into another car right after a firefight does not work for 2 minutes. |
| Hurting AI blows cover | `damageBlows` | on |  | When a covered unit (or its vehicle) hurts an AI soldier, that soldier's group reacts. |
| Victims must see the attacker | `damageNeedsLOS` | on |  | On = a group hurt by someone it did not see only starts SEARCHING. Off = it identifies the attacker anyway. |
| Unseen attack suspicion (%) | `damageSuspicion` | 70 | 0 - 99 | Suspicion given to a group hurt by an attacker it did not see. |
| AI shooting your vehicle = identified | `vehicleAttackedBlows` | on |  | If enemy AI shoot a covered vehicle anyway (it looked dangerous), they identify its occupants. |
| Identify the whole crew | `compromiseCrew` | off |  | Identifying one person in a vehicle identifies everyone undercover in it. |
| Knowledge on identification | `revealKA` | 3 | 0.5 - 4 | How much the AI know about you once identified (0-4, the engine's knowsAbout). 4 = they know exactly where you are. |

## Safe Zones and Truce

| Setting | Name | Default | Range / options | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Safe zones hold a truce | `truceEnabled` | on |  | Inside a Safe haven zone the AI do not attack players of the zone's sides, not even on foot or once identified, as long as the players behave. Made for roleplay areas (Zeus playing the locals). Off = safe zones only stop suspicion from building. |
| Allowed stay (s) | `truceMaxStay` | 0 | 0 - 7200 | How long players may stay in a safe zone before the truce ends. 0 = no limit. Each zone can set its own value in the Zone module. |
| Warning before the end (s) | `truceWarn` | 0 | 0 - 600 | Players get a warning this long before their allowed stay runs out. |
| AI relax inside safe zones | `truceCareless` | on |  | AI groups standing in a safe zone are CARELESS and hold fire until the truce is broken. |
| Who loses the truce | `truceBreakScope` | The offender's group | Only the offender / The offender's group / Everyone in the zone | When one player breaks the truce (shooting, hurting or ramming AI, overstaying)... |
| Aiming at AI breaks the truce | `truceBreakOnAim` | on |  | Pointing a weapon at an AI soldier for the time below breaks the truce. |
| Aiming time (s) | `truceAimTime` | 9.82227 | 1 - 30 | How long aiming at an AI soldier is tolerated. |
| Truce cooldown (s) | `truceCooldown` | 300 | 0 - 3600 | After a break, the players who lost the truce cannot get it back for this long, even by leaving and re-entering. |
| Exit grace (s) | `truceExitGrace` | 10 | 0 - 120 | The truce lasts this long after leaving the zone, so the AI do not open fire at the border. |
| Break reaction radius (m) | `truceBreakRadius` | 200 | 0 - 2000 | Besides the groups inside the zone, groups within this distance of the offender (or seeing them) react. |
| Breaking the truce triggers a bulletin | `truceBulletin` | on |  | Groups reacting to a broken truce roll for a radio bulletin (see 'Radio Bulletins'). |

## Memory and Forgetting

| Setting | Name | Default | Range / options | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Forget after (s) | `forgetAfter` | 180 | 10 - 1800 | A group that identified you forgets you after not seeing you this long, and your disguise works again. |
| Calm at (%) | `recoverThreshold` | 10 | 0 - 50 | SUSPICIOUS or SEARCHING groups calm down (UNAWARE) once suspicion falls below this. |
| Memory after leaving the vehicle (s) | `memoryTime` | 600 | 0 - 3600 | Suspicion is remembered this long after you get out, so getting out and back in does not reset it. |
| Getting out in view reveals at (%) | `exitRevealThreshold` | 74.8879 | 0 - 100 | Getting out of the vehicle in view of a group at or above this suspicion reveals you to it. |
| Age knowledge after losing contact | `targetAge` | Disabled | Disabled / Actual / 5 min / 10 min / 15 min / 30 min / 60 min / Unknown | Optionally ages what EVERY side knows about an identified unit after it breaks contact (setTargetAge). |
| Age knowledge after (s) | `targetAgeDelay` | 60 | 5 - 600 | Time without contact before the knowledge is aged. |

## Sharing and Suspicion Sync

| Setting | Name | Default | Range / options | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| On identification, nearby groups... | `shareMode` | Start searching | Learn nothing / Start searching / Identify too | What friendly groups around learn when a group identifies someone. |
| Share radius (m) | `shareRadius` | 300 | 0 - 3000 | Friendly groups within this distance of any member of the identifying group get the information. |
| Share delay (s) | `shareDelay` | 10.3202 | 0 - 120 | Time before the information arrives. Killing the whole group first stops it. |
| Shared knowledge | `shareKA` | 2 | 0.1 - 4 | How much receiving groups learn about the position (0-4) on a full share. |
| Shared suspicion (%) | `shareSuspicion` | 49.6826 | 0 - 99 | Starting suspicion for groups that start searching. |
| Sharing needs a radio | `shareNeedsRadio` | on |  | The identifying group needs a soldier with a radio to share. |
| Right next to it (m) | `shareInstantRadius` | 150 | 0 - 1000 | Groups this close to an identifying group see the reaction and identify at once. 0 = off. |
| Suspicious groups confirm | `shareEscalate` | on |  | A group already SUSPICIOUS or SEARCHING identifies the unit when it hears about it. |
| Identified vehicle is known | `burnOnIdentify` | on |  | The vehicle someone was identified in is recognised on sight by that side nearby (see range). |
| Known vehicle range (m) | `burnOnIdentifyRange` | 1500 | 0 - 10000 | Distance from the identification within which that side recognises the vehicle. 0 = everywhere. |
| Sync suspicion between groups | `syncEnabled` | on |  | While suspicion builds, nearby friendly groups get the same level after the sync delay. Example: the guards at a checkpoint's exit are as wary as the ones who watched you arrive. Changing vehicle, uniform, vest, helmet or weapon in between shakes it off. |
| Sync radius (m) | `syncRadius` | -1 | -1 - 3000 | Groups within this distance of any member of the sending group receive it. -1 = use 'Share radius'. |
| Sync delay (s) | `syncDelay` | 5 | 0 - 120 | Time for the information to pass (radio, shouting). Killing the senders first stops it. |
| Sync every (s) | `syncInterval` | 3 | 1 - 60 | How often a group passes on rising suspicion. Lower = closer to real time, more network traffic. |
| Synced share | `syncFactor` | 100% | 0-100% | Share of the sender's suspicion the receivers take. 1 = the same level. 0.5 = half. |
| Sync from (%) | `syncMin` | 10 | 0 - 99 | Suspicion below this is not passed on. |
| Sync needs a radio | `syncNeedsRadio` | on |  | The sending group needs a soldier with a radio. |
| Synced suspicion can identify | `syncCanIdentify` | off |  | Off = synced suspicion stops just below 'Identified at', the receivers still need their own look. |
| Changing looks shakes it off | `syncRespectSig` | on |  | Synced suspicion only sticks while you still have the same vehicle and kit the sender saw. |
| Suspicion kept after changing looks | `appearanceChangeKeep` | 35% | 0-100% | When a group sees you again in another vehicle or kit, it keeps this share of its suspicion. 1 = changing makes no difference. 0 = a complete fresh start. |

## Radio Bulletins

| Setting | Name | Default | Range / options | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Radio bulletins | `bulletinEnabled` | on |  | On identification a radioman may broadcast you and your vehicle over a long range. |
| Bulletin chance | `bulletinChance` | 10% | 0-100% | Chance per identifying group that a bulletin is sent. |
| Also after shooting / attacks | `bulletinOnHostile` | on |  | Groups that identified you because of gunfire or attacks also roll. |
| Who can send | `radiomanMode` | Radioman or any radio | Radioman only / Radioman or any radio / Group leader only / Anyone | Which soldiers can send a bulletin. |
| Radio backpacks | `radioBackpacks` | `B_RadioBag_01_base_F,TFAR_Bag_Base,ACRE_PRC117F,ACRE_PRC77` |  | Comma-separated backpack classes that make a radioman (child classes included). |
| Radioman classes | `radiomanClasses` | (empty) |  | Comma-separated unit classes that count as radiomen. Classes with 'radio' in the name always count. |
| Bulletin delay min (s) | `bulletinDelayMin` | 10 | 0 - 300 | Shortest time to send. Killing or knocking out the radioman first cancels it. |
| Bulletin delay max (s) | `bulletinDelayMax` | 30 | 0 - 600 | Longest time to send. |
| Bulletin range (m) | `bulletinRange` | 5000 | 0 - 30000 | Groups farther from the sender do not hear it. 0 = the whole side. |
| Bulletin makes the vehicle known | `bulletinBurn` | on |  | Receiving groups recognise the vehicle on sight and attack its covered occupants. |
| Known vehicle duration (s) | `burnDuration` | 900 | 30 - 7200 | How long a reported vehicle stays known. |
| Bulletin makes you wanted | `bulletinWanted` | on |  | The receiving side builds suspicion faster against you in any vehicle. |
| Wanted duration (s) | `wantedDuration` | 600 | 30 - 7200 | How long the wanted status lasts. |
| Wanted multiplier | `wantedMult` | 2 | 1 - 10 | Suspicion speed against wanted units. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast. |
| Bulletin alerts the area | `bulletinAreaAlert` | on |  | Groups near the reported position start SEARCHING. |
| Area alert radius (m) | `areaAlertRadius` | 600 | 0 - 5000 | Radius around the reported position. |
| Alerts make AI alert | `areaAlertAware` | on |  | Alerted SAFE / CARELESS groups switch to AWARE. |

## Convoys

| Setting | Name | Default | Range / options | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Recognise convoys | `convoyEnabled` | on |  | Undercover vehicles driving close together in the same direction count as one convoy. |
| Convoy gap (m) | `convoyGap` | 100 | 10 - 300 | Vehicles within this distance of each other (chains count) form a convoy. |
| Convoy forms after (s) | `convoyFormTime` | 10 | 0 - 120 | Vehicles must stay together this long before they count as a convoy (two cars meeting at a junction do not). |
| Extra suspicion per vehicle in view | `convoyBuildPerVeh` | 0.15 | 0 - 1 | Each additional convoy vehicle the group can see adds this to the suspicion speed. Example: 0.15 = three vehicles in view build 1.3x as fast. |
| Convoy multiplier cap | `convoyBuildMax` | 1.75 | 1 - 5 | The convoy multiplier never goes above this. |
| One vehicle identified, the rest... | `convoyMode` | Become suspects | Nothing / Become suspects / Are identified too | What happens to the other vehicles of a convoy when one of them is identified (by that group). |
| Spill-over suspicion (%) | `convoySpillSusp` | 60 | 0 - 99 | Suspicion the other convoy vehicles get when 'Become suspects' is chosen. |

## Pursuit and Checkpoint Stops

| Setting | Name | Default | Range / options | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AI pursue suspects | `pursuitEnabled` | on |  | Suspicious and searching groups go after the vehicle with real waypoints: foot patrols run at it, mounted patrols follow it, signal it to stop and inspect it. Their own route resumes afterwards. |
| Pursue from the follow threshold | `followEnabled` | on |  | Groups start a pursuit once their suspicion reaches the follow threshold (searching groups always may). |
| Follow threshold (%) | `followThreshold` | 75 | 1 - 99 | Suspicion at which a group starts following or chasing you instead of just watching. |
| Pursuers per target | `pursuitMaxGroups` | 2 | 1 - 10 | Most groups that pursue the same unit at once. Keeps the whole map from converging on you. |
| Start distance (m) | `pursuitMaxStart` | 600 | 50 - 3000 | Only groups within this distance start a pursuit. |
| Cooldown between pursuits (s) | `pursuitCooldown` | 60 | 0 - 1800 | After a pursuit ends (given up, cleared or called off) that group starts no new one for this long. A passed inspection additionally clears you for 'Cleared for'. |
| Give up after (s) | `pursuitMaxTime` | 180 | 30 - 1800 | A pursuit that has not led to a stop is abandoned after this long. |
| Give up beyond (m) | `pursuitMaxDist` | 1000 | 100 - 10000 | A pursuit is abandoned once the group is this far from where it started. |
| Aim ahead (s) | `pursuitLead` | 2 | 0 - 10 | Pursuers head for where the vehicle will be in this many seconds. |
| Roam limit | `leashEnabled` | on |  | Pursuing groups never go farther than the limits below from where they were (their post or patrol spot). At the edge they stop, and give up and radio if you stay beyond it. Each group can have its own limit (AI Group Profile module / setGroupProfile). |
| Roam limit on foot (m) | `leashFoot` | 200 | 25 - 3000 | How far a foot group may go from home while chasing, searching or inspecting. |
| Roam limit mounted (m) | `leashVehicle` | 600 | 50 - 10000 | How far a mounted group may go from home while following you. |
| Give up beyond the limit after (s) | `leashGiveUp` | 15 | 1 - 300 | You stay beyond their roam limit this long and they give up (and alert, see 'Alert when you get away'). |
| Foot patrols give up at (m) | `footGiveUpDist` | 300 | 50 - 2000 | A foot patrol gives up once the vehicle is this far away (they cannot catch a car). |
| Hold suspicion during a stop request | `stopFreeze` | on |  | A vehicle patrol that starts following you stops judging you: suspicion is held at the follow threshold while they follow and signal you to pull over. It builds normally again once you refuse (the time to stop runs out), pull away from them or open fire / ram anyone. Stopping lets them inspect you instead. Off = suspicion keeps building while they follow (they usually identify you before you can react). |
| Signal to stop within (m) | `stopSignalRange` | 150 | 20 - 500 | A pursuing vehicle starts honking and flashing its lights once it is this close. The time to stop starts then. Example: 150 = the signal starts while they are still a few car lengths behind. |
| Inspect when stopped within (m) | `followDistance` | 40 | 10 - 200 | Stopping while the pursuers are this close starts the inspection. Stopped farther away, they drive up first. |
| Signal every (s) | `stopSignalInterval` | 4 | 4 - 20 | How often the pursuers repeat the signal: two honks 1 s apart and three flashes of the headlights (0.5 s on, 0.5 s off) each time; one signal takes 3 s. Lower = more insistent. Example: 4 with a 30 s time to stop = about 7 signals. |
| Stop signal: horn | `stopSignalHorn` | on |  | Pursuing vehicles honk to make you stop. |
| Stop signal: flashing lights | `stopSignalLights` | on |  | Pursuing vehicles flash their headlights to make you stop. |
| Time to stop (s) | `stopTimeout` | 30 | 5 - 300 | How long the pursuers keep signalling, counted once they are under way and within signal range. Not stopping by then counts as refusing: they radio an alert and suspicion builds normally again. |
| Pulling away counts as fleeing (m) | `stopFleeDistance` | 150 | 50 - 2000 | Getting this much farther from the pursuers than the closest they came (once they are under way) counts as fleeing the stop: they radio an alert and suspicion builds normally again. Example: 150 = they closed to 40 m, you are now 190 m ahead. |
| Refusing to stop adds (%) | `refuseSuspBonus` | 20 | 0 - 99 | Suspicion added to the pursuers when you refuse to stop. |
| Alert when you get away | `alertOnEscape` | on |  | When a pursuit is given up (you were too fast or too far), the pursuers alert the area too. |
| Alert radius (m) | `alertRadius` | 1500 | 0 - 10000 | Groups and outposts within this distance of the pursuers hear their alerts. |
| Alert suspicion (%) | `alertSuspicion` | 60 | 0 - 99 | Groups hearing an alert start SEARCHING with at least this suspicion. |
| Inspect within (m) | `inspectRange` | 30 | 5 - 100 | A foot patrol starts its inspection when your vehicle stops within this distance. |
| Inspection length (s) | `inspectTime` | 30 | 5 - 300 | How long the inspection lasts. Survive it without being identified and you are cleared. |
| Inspection judges the vehicle, not the wait | `inspectCalm` | on |  | During an inspection, standing next to them builds no suspicion: that is the point of a stop. Only what they find counts: a turned-out or exposed occupant, a weapon or turret pointed at them, visible damage, an uncovered occupant, a weapon light or honking. Off = suspicion builds face to face as usual. |
| Inspection multiplier | `inspectMult` | 1.5 | 0.1 - 5 | Suspicion speed while being inspected, once something gives you away (on top of face-to-face). 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast. |
| Clean inspection lowers suspicion by (%) | `inspectClearReduce` | 25 | 0 - 100 | Passing an inspection cleanly lowers that group's suspicion by this much (and never leaves it above 'Cleared suspicion'). Nearby friendly groups get the same value through the sync. Example: 25 with 60% suspicion -> 35%, then capped at 'Cleared suspicion'. |
| Cleared suspicion (%) | `inspectClearSusp` | 15 | 0 - 99 | Highest suspicion left after passing an inspection. 99 = only the reduction above applies. |
| Inspectors | `inspectDismount` | 2 | 1 - 10 | How many of a vehicle patrol get out to inspect, in this order: passengers, other crew without a weapon, the commander, the driver. Gunners never leave their weapon. |
| Crew remount before engaging | `inspectRemount` | on |  | If you flee or get identified during an inspection, dismounted driver / commander / turret crew run back to their own seats first, then the vehicle goes after you. Passengers fight on foot. Off = everyone stays where they are and fights. |
| Cleared for (s) | `inspectCooldown` | 300 | 0 - 3600 | After passing an inspection that group will not pursue you again for this long. |
| Fleeing distance (m) | `fleeDistance` | 25 | 5 - 200 | Driving more than this far from where you stopped, during the inspection, counts as fleeing. |
| Fleeing speed (km/h) | `fleeSpeed` | 15 | 3 - 100 | Driving faster than this during the inspection counts as fleeing. |
| Fleeing sends a bulletin | `fleeBulletin` | Always | Never / By chance / Always | Fleeing a stop gets you identified on the spot. Should they also radio a bulletin? |
| Fleeing makes the vehicle known | `fleeBurn` | on |  | The vehicle you fled in is recognised on sight within the bulletin range. |
| LAMBS: hold off during pursuit | `lambsDisableDuringPursuit` | on |  | With LAMBS Danger loaded, its group AI is paused while a group pursues, so it does not break the chase. |
| LAMBS: hunt when identified | `lambsHuntOnCompromise` | on |  | With LAMBS loaded, pursuers that identify you hand over to LAMBS Rush (on foot) or Hunt (mounted). |

## Informants, Theft, Ramming, Plates

| Setting | Name | Default | Range / options | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Civilian informants | `informantsEnabled` | on |  | Civilians who see a soldier get into a vehicle or a hostile act may report it. |
| Informant chance | `informantChance` | 15% | 0-100% | Chance per civilian group that witnesses it. |
| Informant delay (s) | `informantDelay` | 45 | 0 - 600 | Time to make the report. Cancelled if the informant dies. |
| Informant range (m) | `informantRange` | 200 | 10 - 1000 | How far away a civilian can witness from. |
| Stolen vehicles are known | `theftEnabled` | on |  | Taking a vehicle last used by an AI group makes it known to that side if the owners are near or see it. |
| Theft witness radius (m) | `theftRadius` | 50 | 0 - 500 | Owners within this distance always notice the theft. |
| Detect ramming | `ramDetect` | on |  | Driving into or over enemy soldiers alerts their group at once. |
| Ramming from (km/h) | `ramSpeed` | 5 | 1 - 60 | Minimum speed for contact to count as ramming. |
| Ramming suspicion (%) | `ramSuspicion` | 75 | 0 - 99 | Suspicion the rammed group has at least after being rammed (at least SUSPICIOUS). A single ram only does this; ramming again does what 'Ramming = identified' says. |
| Full reaction from ram # | `ramRepeatCount` | 2 | 1 - 10 | A single bump can be an accident: the first rams only raise suspicion (Ramming suspicion). From this ram on (by the same vehicle, against the same group, within the window) 'Ramming = identified' applies. Example: 2 = the second ram gets you identified. 1 = the first one already does. |
| Repeated ramming window (s) | `ramRepeatWindow` | 300 | 10 - 1800 | Rams count as repeated when the next comes within this long of the last one. |
| Ramming = identified | `ramCompromise` | on |  | Ramming again (see 'Full reaction from ram #') - a soldier, or their vehicle - gets everyone undercover in your vehicle identified by that group at once. Off = the group only becomes SUSPICIOUS (see Ramming suspicion). |
| Ramming makes the vehicle known | `ramBurn` | on |  | The ramming vehicle is recognised on sight by that side (within 'Known vehicle range'), so swapping crews does not save it. |
| Fresh vehicle after being identified | `swapForgive` | on |  | An identified unit that switches to another vehicle unseen is only suspected again, not identified. The old vehicle stays known. |
| Unseen before switching (s) | `swapMinUnseen` | 15 | 0 - 300 | The group must not have seen you for this long (and must not see you now) when you switch. |
| Suspicion after switching (%) | `swapBaseSuspicion` | 30 | 0 - 99 | Starting suspicion after the first switch. |
| Repeat switch penalty (%) | `swapPenalty` | 30 | 0 - 100 | Extra starting suspicion for every earlier switch. Once it reaches 'Identified at', switching no longer works. |
| Switch memory (s) | `swapMemory` | 900 | 60 - 7200 | How long a group remembers earlier switches. |
| Recognise reported number plates | `plateRecognition` | on |  | A reported vehicle's number plate is reported too: any vehicle with that plate is identified as soon as the plate is read, whatever its side. |
| Plate reading range (m) | `plateReadRange` | 50 | 5 - 300 | Soldiers must be this close (with line of sight) to read a plate. |
| Reported plate = COMBAT | `plateCombat` | on |  | A group that reads a reported plate goes COMBAT at once. |

## AI Reactions

| Setting | Name | Default | Range / options | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Suspicious groups go alert | `aiAware` | on |  | SAFE / CARELESS groups switch to AWARE while suspicious, and back when calm. |
| AI glance at new vehicles | `aiGlance` | on |  | The soldier who first notices your vehicle glances at it (they turn their head, so they see more). |
| Suspicious AI keep looking | `aiLook` | on |  | Once suspicious, the best placed soldier keeps looking at your vehicle until the group calms down. |
| Suspicious groups watch you | `aiWatch` | on |  | Every soldier of a suspicious group turns to watch the vehicle (stronger than looking). |
| Identifying groups go COMBAT | `aiCombatOnIdentify` | on |  | Groups that identify you switch to COMBAT. |

## Debug

| Setting | Name | Default | Range / options | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Who may use debug | `debugClients` | Admins and Zeus | Logged-in admins / Admins and Zeus / Everyone | Server permission for the per-player debug options below (log, overlay, live publishing). The server and headless clients always may. Players outside this list have them switched off whatever they set, so nobody can watch AI suspicion on their own. |
| Debug log *(per player)* | `debugLog` | on |  | Writes every RADS decision to the RPT of the machine that owns the AI (server / headless client) and of the player: identifications with full history, state changes, ramming, hits, shots, shares, syncs, truces, pursuits, cover changes. |
| Debug log detail *(per player)* | `debugDetail` | Every evaluation | Events and reports / Also big jumps / Every evaluation | What is logged besides events and identification reports. |
| Big jump from (%) *(per player)* | `debugJump` | 8 | 1 - 100 | With 'Also big jumps', an evaluation adding at least this much is logged. |
| History length *(per player)* | `debugHistory` | 15 | 1 - 60 | Evaluations kept per group and unit and printed with every report. |
| Publish suspicion live *(per player)* | `debugPublish` | on |  | Group owners broadcast suspicion every evaluation so overlays and Zeus Inspect stay live. Costs network traffic. |
| Debug overlay *(per player)* | `debugOverlay` | on |  | Draws every nearby group's suspicion of you over its closest member (needs 'Publish suspicion live'). Per player. |
| Show zone markers | `showZoneMarkers` | on |  | Creates map markers for detection zones (visible to everyone). |
